status: World and room authoring guide; only the depot is currently playable

setting.name: The Lumen Reach
setting.premise: People live among floating stone islands joined by root bridges, light canals and a worn star-post network. They maintain beautiful old machines whose makers are gone.
setting.bell: The public bell once synchronized doors, dispatch routes, water clocks and courier birds. Its silence disrupts those shared routines; it does not make the islands fall.
setting.magicAndTechnology: Crystal cells, living roots and carefully timed phrases operate the same inherited machinery. A kitchen lamp and a distant route beacon use related parts at very different scales.
setting.mystery: The old bellkeeper’s parcel returns with warm wax while the outgoing route lamps are dark. Evidence should deepen the question before any character claims to know its answer.
setting.humanScale: Keep the world legible through work, meals, repairs, gardens, deliveries and small promises. Wonder and absence carry the tone; no immediate catastrophe or violent threat is required.

visualRules: Keep the chosen Pocket Pixel proportions, large readable clusters, warm dark outlines and limited material shading.
Use orthographic 2/3 views with parallel edges and consistent scale. Furniture and floor edges do not converge toward a vanishing point.
Pair high-fantasy forms with obsolete future machinery: moonstone arches around curved phosphor glass, root-wrapped copper conduits, star-glass cells in hand-repaired ceramic housings.
Show one strong room landmark, a visible daily routine and a trace of something older. Leave navigable floor and keep doors, people and useful objects readable.
Show systems visibly connecting: root into conduit, conduit into machine, machine into the thing it helps someone do. Do not scatter unrelated glowing props as decoration.
Use rings, arcs, comets, constellations and musical waveforms. Avoid religious or occult signs, gore, grim violence and writing on the floor.

Give each branch its own materials and light: garden jade and amber, workshop teal and copper, canal indigo and pearl. Small warm lights and local crystal cells can remain active while the main network is quiet.
authoringRules: This file adds setting and environmental storytelling; dungeon.json remains the authority for room IDs, sources, door costs, reveal conditions and ending budgets.
Every room must answer who uses it, what they do here, what has changed and what might lie beyond the visible space.
Inspection copy is a short observation before an explanation. Physical evidence should support personal dialogue rather than repeat an encyclopedia entry.
An environmental clue can allude to a different route without adding a room or edge to the discovered chart.
Inspections supply no notes, unlock no paid door, grant no party promise and do not count as outcomes. Any future resource source must be authored and verified separately.
Only entered rooms and travelled connections enter the journey chart. No unread prop, hidden room title, total or planned ending is exposed by the authoring catalog.

rooms.title: The Parcel Depot
rooms.occupation: A neighborhood post station built inside a former sky-survey hall.
rooms.landmark: An old route orrery whose carriage slows for a polished-away star.
rooms.everydayHabit: Nell keeps one service lamp lit and checks the reply tray; Pip leaves seed for a mechanical courier.
rooms.traceOfPast: Survey rings and disconnected bell relays remain above newer parcel shelves and hand-repaired terminals.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: How did the bellkeeper’s parcel return warm when the outgoing route lamps are dark?
rooms.routeClue: Three visibly different door systems serve living roots, clockwork birds and waterborne deliveries. Their residents know their distinct phrases.

props.title: The warm returned letter
props.observation: A warm wax seal and several forwarding labels end with the depot’s own star stamp.
props.purpose: Establish the personal delivery mystery.

props.title: A courier waiting for a reply
props.observation: Real seed rests beside a brass bird whose crystal throat clicks toward an unlit route.
props.purpose: Show Pip’s care and the network’s missing answer.

props.title: The sleeping dispatch map
props.observation: A thumb-worn button starts a luminous route that stops before its return signal.
props.purpose: Show how the bell once coordinated ordinary work.

props.title: The star that was rubbed away
props.observation: A carriage still slows for a stop erased from its brass ring.
props.purpose: Suggest that the inherited network remembers more than its current labels.

props.title: The star-post receiver
props.observation: A local crystal lights the receiver beside a disconnected main relay and a worn reply socket.
props.purpose: Connect local life, old machinery and the unexplained returned delivery.

rooms.title: Iris’s Garden Porch
rooms.occupation: A gardener’s work porch where living roots are grafted into the island’s old service conduits.
rooms.landmark: A crystal irrigation manifold wrapped by one carefully tended living root.
rooms.everydayHabit: Iris sets out two cups before watering the beds and moves the second chair out of the rain.
rooms.traceOfPast: A formal survey conduit has been repaired with garden twine and labeled seed jars.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Who taught Iris to leave a pause for an answer that does not come?
rooms.routeClue: The listening gate waits through two quiet beats before answering; the overgrown arch offers an older, poorly tended call.

props.title: The second cup
props.observation: The empty place has a dry cloth and a cup with a recently mended handle.
props.purpose: Make the absent duet partner part of a living routine.

props.title: The patient graft
props.observation: A green shoot pulses only after the copper pipe falls quiet.
props.purpose: Give a material example of waiting before a reply.

props.title: The reused survey plaque
props.observation: A once-important machine plate now supports a row of small seedlings.
props.purpose: Show how residents have made old systems useful again.

rooms.title: Pip’s Bird Workshop
rooms.occupation: A small repair shop and roost for the star-post’s clockwork courier birds.
rooms.landmark: A nest-shaped charging cradle suspended inside an open brass wing.
rooms.everydayHabit: Pip sorts spare feathers by flight shape and keeps a bowl of seed beside his trays of gears.
rooms.traceOfPast: The roost was once one station in a much larger migration system; its smallest perches have been lowered for Pip’s repairs.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Why does one repaired bird turn away from every route currently marked on the board?
rooms.routeClue: A long movement divides into two quick replies and then four tiny ones; the birds decline to answer the silent aviary.

props.title: The practice wing
props.observation: A test jig moves once, twice and then four times, leaving Pip’s fingertips stained with copper polish.
props.purpose: Connect the workshop’s rhythm to practiced work.

props.title: The unnecessary seed bowl
props.observation: Fresh husks surround birds that run on crystal cells.
props.purpose: Show Pip treating his couriers as companions.

props.title: The unmatched feather
props.observation: One pale metal feather does not fit any of the birds on the bench.
props.purpose: Suggest a missing member of a larger flock.

rooms.title: The Canal Storehouse
rooms.occupation: A ferry keeper’s freight store beside a light canal that carries parcels between floating islands.
rooms.landmark: A closed tide iris reflected in still luminous water.
rooms.everydayHabit: The ferry keeper dries postage seals on a line and warms tea on a small local crystal heater.
rooms.traceOfPast: A sky-navigation console is bolted to a practical wooden loading desk.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Why is one returned delivery damp with water from a route the ferry no longer serves?
rooms.routeClue: The stamped chest and delivery gate share a long stroke, an ordinary tap and a paired reply; the abandoned boarding rope offers no waiting boat.

props.title: The drying seals
props.observation: Ordinary household parcels hang beside a seal carrying an unfamiliar pale tide mark.
props.purpose: Keep the strange network attached to daily deliveries.

props.title: The secondhand navigator
props.observation: A polished steering control has been repaired with ferry rope and a wooden wedge.
props.purpose: Show future machinery inherited and adapted by working people.

props.title: The small mooring bell
props.observation: Its clapper is tied safely aside, waiting for the keeper to hear the proper return knock.
props.purpose: Explain the keeper’s caution and the importance of an answering phrase.

rooms.title: The Two Garden Paths
rooms.occupation: A shared growing court where a new neighborhood path meets the buried route of an older garden.
rooms.landmark: A split root bridge: one side freshly tended, the other following worn stone beneath the leaves.
rooms.everydayHabit: Neighbors have hung repaired watering cans and herb bundles where everyone can borrow them.
rooms.traceOfPast: An ornamental paving ring continues below a newer domestic walkway.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: What was the old garden listening to before houses were built along its edge?
rooms.routeClue: A long call and an ordinary step suit the hearth path; the older path is marked by smaller replies with a breath between them.

props.title: The shared watering can
props.observation: Several different hands have repaired the same handle.
props.purpose: Make the homeward branch feel cared for and communal.

props.title: The buried paving ring
props.observation: Its worn grooves pass beneath roots instead of following the newer path.
props.purpose: Give the older route a material history.

props.title: The listening cups
props.observation: Small ceramic cups answer a breeze only after one empty space in their row.
props.purpose: Recall the value of an intentional rest without revealing an unseen gate.

rooms.title: The Workshop Crossroads
rooms.occupation: A narrow makers’ exchange between public teaching rooms and the old backstage service spaces.
rooms.landmark: A suspended demonstration bird above two different generations of doorway.
rooms.everydayHabit: Apprentices leave unfinished mechanisms on a shelf for the next person to help repair.
rooms.traceOfPast: A neat classroom stair has been fitted into a much older performance machine.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Who used the narrow rear passage when the public music room was closed?
rooms.routeClue: The public stair carries an extended call and one ordinary reply; the back passage has long quiet spaces before its small returning sounds.

props.title: The help shelf
props.observation: An unfinished bird has three different styles of careful repair around the same wing.
props.purpose: Show teaching as shared practical work.

props.title: The back rail
props.observation: Dust fills the middle of the rail, but the handholds at either end are bright.
props.purpose: Make the quieter route feel used rather than arbitrary.

props.title: The silent sound screen
props.observation: A curved phosphor display keeps space between the last two small pulses.
props.purpose: Tie the passage’s rhythm to a physical instrument.

rooms.title: The Water Clock
rooms.occupation: A public timing chamber that once synchronized ferry tides with the town bell.
rooms.landmark: A tall water clock with suspended drops waiting above a dry answering bowl.
rooms.everydayHabit: Someone has left a stool and a folded towel beside the clock’s service hatch.
rooms.traceOfPast: The chamber’s oldest conduits continue beyond a carefully drawn modern maintenance map.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Why does the imitation channel repeat the clock perfectly but never carry a reply back?
rooms.routeClue: The town-bell stair follows a sustained call and four quick footfalls; a copied waterway reflects a familiar quiet phrase but ends against stone.

props.title: The waiting drop
props.observation: The clock holds one silver drop until the empty bowl receives its answer.
props.purpose: Show the failure as a missing conversation between machines.

props.title: The keeper’s stool
props.observation: A cushion and repaired footrest make a long watch a little kinder.
props.purpose: Give the maintenance worker a life beyond the puzzle.

props.title: The practical maintenance map
props.observation: The keeper has plainly marked the copied channel’s solid end.
props.purpose: Provide a fair visible warning for the intentional dead end.

rooms.title: The Hearth Bell
rooms.occupation: A small neighborhood hall where domestic lamps and kitchen chimes share a bell relay.
rooms.landmark: A modest bell hanging inside the frame of an oversized ancient relay.
rooms.everydayHabit: Residents leave cups warming and set out an extra place for whoever comes through next.
rooms.traceOfPast: A machine designed for a far larger place has been made into a useful home fixture.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Was the old network built to reach great distances, or to help people answer one another nearby?
rooms.routeClue: The remaining small groups, breath and short replies complete a phrase made for a shared home.

props.title: The extra place
props.observation: The chair is empty, but its cup is warm and its cushion has been straightened.
props.purpose: Pay off the branch’s attention to welcome and absence.

props.title: The kitchen relay
props.observation: A formidable old switch now turns a tiny soup warmer on and off.
props.purpose: Show ordinary lives determining the use of old power.

props.title: The mended clapper
props.observation: Several household repair methods meet at the same small bell.
props.purpose: Make the final answer a communal achievement.

rooms.title: The Open Music Room
rooms.occupation: A community teaching room rebuilt around a retired star-navigation instrument.
rooms.landmark: A great circular navigator converted into a shared listening instrument.
rooms.everydayHabit: Low stools, finger-smudged practice controls and spare parts are ready for learners of different sizes.
rooms.traceOfPast: The old instrument’s ceremonial controls have been lowered and fitted with simple wooden grips.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: How much of the old machinery can people understand by learning to listen together?
rooms.routeClue: Two quiet beats, another quiet beat and two different short replies leave room for an answering voice.

props.title: The lowered control
props.observation: A wooden extension lets the smallest stool reach the oldest brass lever.
props.purpose: Show the room was adapted for real learners.

props.title: The practice patches
props.observation: Different repaired cloth squares mark places where people learned by trying again.
props.purpose: Make mistakes part of the room’s lived history.

props.title: The listening ring
props.observation: Its empty centre faces the other seats instead of a lone operator’s desk.
props.purpose: Turn grand technology toward shared musical play.

rooms.title: The Evening Tower
rooms.occupation: The public bell tower and the working heart of the town’s old timing network.
rooms.landmark: A silent bell above a circle of dark route lamps, with the inhabited islands visible beyond.
rooms.everydayHabit: A keeper has left a patched coat, a broom and a flask beside an immense service instrument.
rooms.traceOfPast: The tower connects household-sized repairs to a system that spans the Reach.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: What does a public signal owe the people who depend on it?
rooms.routeClue: The final phrase leaves long and short spaces before its small replies, making the room ready to hear the town answer.

props.title: The waiting lamps
props.observation: Each dark lamp has been cleaned as carefully as the one that still glows.
props.purpose: Show care for distant neighbors without listing undiscovered game routes.

props.title: The keeper’s flask
props.observation: The flask fits a hand-sized shelf added to a machine of enormous scale.
props.purpose: Keep the tower inhabited and human in scale.

props.title: The reply dish
props.observation: Its centre faces outward toward the islands, waiting to receive as well as send.
props.purpose: Express the importance of the answer rather than simply restoring power.

rooms.title: The Overgrown Music Box
rooms.occupation: An old root-service nook whose maintenance instrument has become part of the garden.
rooms.landmark: A flower-carved stone above a music box that roots have grown around without crushing.
rooms.everydayHabit: A small cleared patch and carefully moved leaves show that someone still tends this forgotten corner.
rooms.traceOfPast: An older maintenance phrase survives inside the music box rather than on a modern route sign.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Who kept this place ready for a visitor who might never come?
rooms.routeClue: The loose flower stone and the instrument beneath it must be discovered here; their note source and hidden reveal remain the authored once-only actions.

props.title: The cleared patch
props.observation: Freshly turned leaves protect a dry place beside the old stone.
props.purpose: Make the detour feel cared for instead of abandoned treasure storage.

props.title: The root cradle
props.observation: Roots curve around the little instrument’s lid, leaving it room to open.
props.purpose: Show living and inherited systems cooperating.

props.title: The flower stone
props.observation: One carved petal is polished by a hand-sized grip.
props.purpose: Make the existing hidden search discoverable through specific physical evidence.

rooms.title: The Birds’ Dusty Attic
rooms.occupation: The old courier roost’s reserve loft, kept above the public workshop.
rooms.landmark: A hollow two-sided perch among unused courier harnesses.
rooms.everydayHabit: Someone has folded old wing wraps and left a small brush beside the quiet perches.
rooms.traceOfPast: Different generations of birds have left differently sized marks along the same roost rail.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Which of the old couriers was meant to use a perch that sounds on only one side?
rooms.routeClue: The hollow perch holds the existing once-only hidden source. One side sounding and one side quiet supports its authored reveal without changing the source budget.

props.title: The folded wing wraps
props.observation: Each wrap has been repaired to fit a different small wing.
props.purpose: Show generations of care above the visible workshop.

props.title: The old roost marks
props.observation: Tiny scratches stop beside larger empty spaces along the rail.
props.purpose: Suggest a courier history wider than the current flock.

props.title: The two-sided perch
props.observation: A gentle tap gives a clear tone on one side and a muffled pause on the other.
props.purpose: Make the hidden search a fair observation rather than an arbitrary click.

rooms.title: The Reserved Room
rooms.occupation: A small listening room deliberately kept apart from the busy shared garden.
rooms.landmark: A carefully maintained empty chair beside a dormant listening window.
rooms.everydayHabit: The room has fresh water, folded cloth and enough space left for someone else’s work.
rooms.traceOfPast: A second set of hand-worn controls has been preserved rather than replaced.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: Can restoring a shared song include leaving an unfinished part unfilled?
rooms.routeClue: The long call and ordinary step carried through the detour belong to the final answer here; the room should reward the player’s earlier care with that inventory.

props.title: The maintained chair
props.observation: Its place is empty, but nothing about it has been neglected.
props.purpose: Distinguish a chosen space from an abandoned one.

props.title: The second controls
props.observation: Two different hands wore the adjacent controls in different ways.
props.purpose: Give Iris’s personal history physical weight.

props.title: The listening window
props.observation: Its receiver faces the garden even while the sending side rests.
props.purpose: Pay off the branch’s attention to listening without naming the outcome in advance.

rooms.title: The Hidden Countermelody
rooms.occupation: A quiet reply chamber behind the courier birds’ performance machinery.
rooms.landmark: A second, smaller listening horn hidden behind the great public sending horn.
rooms.everydayHabit: A little step and a freshly brushed perch let a small bird reach the older mechanism.
rooms.traceOfPast: The system was built to receive a different phrase, not merely repeat the main one.
rooms.unansweredQuestion: What have the birds been trying to add to the town’s song?
rooms.routeClue: The long call and ordinary step saved through the quiet passage complete this answer. The environment should suggest an independent reply without announcing a secret ending.

props.title: The smaller horn
props.observation: Its rim is polished from the inside, as if something small has been speaking into it.
props.purpose: Reveal a practical reason for the chamber’s hidden position.

props.title: The little service step
props.observation: A hand-built step reaches the one control a small courier cannot reach from its perch.
props.purpose: Continue the theme of people adapting inherited machines for one another.

props.title: The two sound traces
props.observation: Two phosphor traces approach the same pause along different curves.
props.purpose: Make an independent voice visible before its final musical payoff.
